Issued at 315 AM CDT Sat Sep 5 2026

The general pattern evolution across the CONUS remains high 
confidence. The LREF 500mb spreads are predominantly < 3 dam across 
CONUS until mid-week. Even then, majority of the increasing spreads 
are understandably seen arcing over the Central and Southern Plains, 
keeping area 500mb spreads <= 3 dam through next week. What does 
this mean? Since we are currently entrenched within mid-level 
ridging, it generally means well above normal temperatures stick 
around through the forecast. For general reference, 30-year normal 
highs are around the low to mid 80s this time of the year. Of 
course, 500mb pattern evolution does not tell the whole story, and 
there are some details within the forecast, aside from heat, worth 
noting, including storm chances, backdoor cold front, and more 
substantial relief later in the forecast. 

The existing Omega block pattern is expected to largely remain 
locked in place through the weekend. While this keeps peak heat 
potential similar to previous few days, in the mid to upper 90s, 
there will be an opportunity for that temperature forecast to bust 
this weekend. Today will not be that day though with light southerly 
flow and a 700 mb temp ridge nosing into the area that will keep any 
air-mass convection from developing. Those chances should remain 
relegated more toward the Ozarks portions of the state where 700mb 
temps are a couple degrees cooler and may allow convective temps to 
be achieved. So mid-upper 90s, even touching 100 possible, for much 
of the area today. By the latter portions of today, a surface high 
dropping into the Great Lakes region will begin to push a backdoor 
cool front (generous wording there) into NE Missouri. This will do a 
couple of things. Most notably it will drop Sunday highs into the 
upper 80s and lower 90s for NE and E Missouri. Unfortunately it 
tends to stall out as it pushes westward across the state, providing 
limited or no relief to areas W and S of a line from around 
Maryville MO to Columbia MO. This results in the end of the Extreme 
Heat Warning for portions of N/NE Missouri Saturday evening, and 
continuing further south through Tuesday. Concurrently, 700mb temps 
will fall across the area, setting the table for the potential for 
some scattered thunderstorm activity near the surface boundary and 
westward where this cooling may allow scattered air-mass convection 
to be achieved. Additionally, shower/storm activity rounding the mid-
level ridge may drop S/SE out of Nebraska/Iowa along the expected 
CAPE axis. Timing for all of this would be Sunday afternoon and into 
the evening. Wind profiles do not support organization, but a very 
dry sub-cloudbase layer could provide opportunities for evaporatively 
enhanced downdrafts. As hinted earlier, this too provides the chance 
for a busted temperature forecast in areas that see storms, 
especially if areal coverage of activity increases. 

By late weekend and into the early work week, the Omega Block begins 
to break down in response to a Polar Stream trough pushing the New 
England cutoff low eastward. The western CONUS cutoff low will take 
advantage and begin to move E/NE itself, eventually yielding surface 
low development over eastern Montana and into the southern Canadian 
Plains. This will also act to push the mid-level ridge back eastward 
and generally begin to flatten. Unfortunately, no notable relief to 
the area, in fact a general brief resurgence of the heat as the 
850mb temp ridge axis angles into the state. Expect temperatures 
Monday to be similar to Sunday, but surge back warmer a few degrees 
on Tuesday back into the upper 90s and around 100 for many. By 
Wednesday, the mid-level ridge flattens and a cold front will begin 
to approach the area from the north. This too is where uncertainty 
begins to increase with some varied timing in arrival time. Slower 
arrival may yield an extension of the Extreme Heat Warning one more 
day, but confidence is not quite there to extend with LREF and NBM 
MaxT spreads of 6 to 10 degrees. Higher confidence in relief (but 
likely still at least a few degrees above normal) by Thursday and to 
end the week though, including potential for some shower/storm 
activity in/around the front as well as shortwave activity.
